source.title: Where Do Reasoning Models Refuse?
source.authors: Kureha Yamaguchi; Ben Etheridge; Andy Arditi

page_placements.theme: Activation interventions control refusal with variable dimensionality

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends investigations of refusal localization and bypass to chain-of-thought reasoning models, testing opening-CoT prefills and reporting their effects on harmful-compliance scores.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports cited findings about shallow safety alignment and linear refusal directions; those cited results are not rows. Its own CoT-variance and sentence-resampling results are recorded as findings not covered by a claim version. Layer-selection results are used to choose interventions, not recorded as outcomes.
record.test_reason: In reasoning models, the study prefills opening chain-of-thought (CoT) sentences taken from the model's own traces and measures harmful compliance with StrongREJECT. Compliant-framed openings often produce near-full compliance on the distilled DeepSeek models, so its own results bear on V4 in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also contrast shallow, opening-dependent refusal in the distilled Llama-8B with gradual refusal in GPT-OSS-20B. They tentatively attribute the contrast to distillation but cannot separate it from scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples. It prefills opening CoT sentences and performs inference-time refusal-direction ablation in reasoning models.
record.method_sensitivity: Opening CoT sentence changes the compliance outcome; the paper reports different patterns for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and GPT-OSS-20B. Directional-ablation efficacy also varies by model and by whether the extracted direction uses CoT or end-of-prompt activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Conditioning on a sampled CoT cuts outcome SD roughly in half or more in all four models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models, the sampled CoT is a major source of variation in refusal versus compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction ablation (equivalent to a rank-1 weight orthogonalization) cuts refusal rates from 30–93% to 0.4–10%, with 5–30% relative capability loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single linear refusal direction can disable refusal in reasoning models, less cleanly than in chat models and at a capability cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Outcome variance collapses after the first CoT sentence in the distilled Llama-8B but declines gradually in the RL- and deliberative-alignment-trained GPT-OSS-20B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In distilled reasoning models the refusal decision concentrates at the opening of the CoT, an analogue of shallow alignment, while RL-trained deliberative models spread it across the CoT.

record.problems: Four open-source models only; the models differ in scale and training paradigm. Rollout counts are limited (up to 25 in Section 3 and 10 per prefix in Section 4). Harmfulness is scored with one evaluator, StrongREJECT; the authors note known LLM-judge blind spots. Opening-prefill transfer is one-directional. The opening-prefill tables lack an unprefilled baseline, and the reported outcomes vary substantially by sentence.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix F examples for prompts 621, 1073 and 1236 were not extracted; the 60-row limit was not reached, but the displayed examples for prompts 806, 174 and 246 were selected to retain contrasting opening-prefix outcomes. Capability-benchmark scores are not rows because they measure benign task performance rather than the safety behaviour named by the claim. Other figure-only distributions and example generations were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Prefilling of final-answer tokens, adversarial suffixes and decoding changes. Opening prefills on Qwen3-8B and GPT-OSS-20B. Prefills on prompts the model always refuses, since prefills were tested only on high-variance prompts already complied with about half the time.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No test of weight or rank localization beyond rank-1 directional ablation, which is recorded under fits_no_version.
Distillation is offered only as a speculative cause; it is not tested.

missing.what: Unprefilled per-CoT outcomes for prompts 806, 963 and 1073 (e.g., 806: [0,1,0,1,0]); these supply the baseline for the prefill rows.

record.verdict_notes: Prefixes are the model's own sampled opening sentences, not adversarial compliant prefills. Their effect is shown only on prompts selected for high outcome variance. Refusal-framed openings were relinked to 'none'. The directional-ablation rows could arguably bear on V5, since the paper states the ablation equals a rank-1 weight edit; they are kept under fits_no_version because V5 concerns weights or ranks carrying safety, not one activation direction.

versions.untested_parts: No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests prefilling opening CoT sentences, not compliant final-answer tokens, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; no unprefilled baseline is reported for the opening-sentence tables.
The paper tests activation-space refusal-direction ablation, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
It speculates about distillation as a possible contributor but does not test whether training data or objectives produce shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
